== Biography ==
Philip Glasgow was baptised on 3 June 1711 at Uphall, West Lothian, Scotland, a son of [[Glasgow-1242|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Duncan-16665|Jean Duncan]].<ref name="Baptism">FamilySearch, “Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” Philip Glasgow, baptised 3 June 1711 at Uphall, father Thomas Glasgow and mother Jean Duncan, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-S7Z record VQ48-S7Z]. This is a derivative index entry.</ref> His structured birth date and place are estimates based on that baptism.

No reviewed record proves that this Scottish child later became a Dublin watchmaker. The Dublin records below are retained as evidence for a possible later identity, not as established events in Philip's life.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1242]] is assessed at 52% (possible). The held account describes Philip baptized 3 June 1711 at Uphall, son of Thomas Glasgow and Jean Duncan; the selected Thomas’s generation and stated Jean Duncan marriage are compatible. However the saved subject label is Mary, while another family citation gives Philip at Linlithgow on 21 October 1711.

Possible for the current profile placement. The two baptism events and Mary/Philip label conflict must be reconciled; neither baptism alone identifies the later Dublin watchmaker. No name, date or parent replacement is applied.

Next useful test: Compare both 1711 register entries and identify which child the profile was intended to represent.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-S7Z Philip at Uphall,3 June 1711: retained Thomas/Jean child index]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

Select Thomas [[Glasgow-1242]] as the uncertain working father of Philip [[Glasco-146]]. The preferred model uses [[Glasco-146]] as the elder Dublin watchmaker account, retaining the 1711 Scottish child [[Glasgow-1241]] as a separate possible account of the same man. That child’s Uphall index names father Thomas; his existing research already retains the elder watchmaker as a compatible adult identity. The [[Glasco-146]] account has the Christ Church Lane watchmaking association in 1752, an estimated birth about 1715 and a younger Philip in its tree family, which suit that provisional elder role. The four-year difference from the 1711 baptism is between a record and an unsupported estimate, not a concrete identity conflict. This materialises the existing Scottish candidate at low confidence; it does not prove migration or two distinct elder Philips.

The Dublin records name no Scottish parents, birthplace or apprenticeship, so the Scottish child and elder watchmaker may be different men. The fresh [[Glasco-146]] biography itself mixes the 1752 watchmaker with junior notices of 1765,1768 and 1770. Its c.1715 birth and the c.1740 birth of [[Glasco-147]] are tree estimates, not evidence selecting a generation. If [[Glasco-146]] instead represents the junior, the elder Philip is an alternative father-generation placement and the Thomas link would need revision; no competing father is attached alongside it. The elder placement is a preferred working interpretation of the profile’s trade/address and family structure, not a claim that every event in that biography belongs to him. The junior’s 1765 unnamed-wife death,1768 Teresa Plunkett marriage and reported 1770 death remain with the younger documentary account [[Glasgow-3932]]. [[Glasco-147]] is a strongly supported duplicate account of that younger man, but its quoted 1772 younger/inventory wording was not independently rechecked here and establishes neither the estimated birth nor a newly verified father clause; a grant date is not a death date. No merge, spouse transfer or new child attachment follows. Catherine Mangan is called [[Glasco-146]]’s mother in its prose but spouse in its structured family; the 1750 report describes the elder’s bride only as the widow Mangan, and the 1760 report gives no forename. Neither record proves maternity. Preserve the existing Mangan/Braccan and younger-parent fields as qualified leads; do not add a mother for [[Glasco-146]]. The father Thomas is common to the retained 1711 child records, while the 3 June Uphall versus 21 October Linlithgow Philip entries and their maternal readings remain unreconciled; Jean Duncan is not transferred as [[Glasco-146]]’s mother. The 1777 probate/court occurrence does not establish survival after 1772. The local elder account uses 1772 as an uncertain death year through the selected identity, retaining the old after 1772 value and all junior events in the comparison.

The Scottish child remains this account’s record-defined starting point; the selected Dublin connection does not prove two distinct elder sons called Philip. === Two Dublin watchmakers ===

Irish records distinguish '''two Dublin watchmakers named Philip Glasco'''. The elder was established in Christ Church Lane by 1750, when a newspaper reported that Philip Glasco senior had married the widow Mangan of County Kildare.<ref name="ProjectSource1">[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/dc1719_52.html ''Dublin Courant'' extraction, 8 May 1750].</ref> His wife died in 1760.<ref name="ProjectSource2">[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/fdj1725_98.html ''Faulkner's Dublin Journal'' extraction, 2 February 1760].</ref>

Philip junior of Christchurch Yard married Teresa Plunkett in 1768.<ref name="ProjectSource3">[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/pg1758_74.html ''Public Gazetteer'' extraction, 17 September 1768].</ref> He died in Christ Church Lane in 1770.<ref name="ProjectSource4">[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/dm1723_73.html ''Dublin Mercury'' extraction, 22 December 1770].</ref> The designation “junior” strongly supports two generations but does not formally name the elder Philip as his father. [[Glasgow-3932|Philip junior]] is therefore retained as an uncertain child.

The Dublin Gazette reported the death of the eminent watchmaker Philip Glasco in October 1772, and the 1772 will index describes Phillip of Dublin as a watchmaker.<ref name="ProjectSource5">[https://virtualtreasury.ie/ ''Dublin Gazette'', 6–8 October 1772, reference DGZ 1772/2547].</ref><ref name="Will1772">Virtual Record Treasury of Ireland, [https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/PROI-DKPRI-26-7 1772 will index], Phillip, Dublin, watchmaker.</ref> These records identify the elder Dublin man, but do not connect him to the Scottish baptism. A separate FamilySearch probate index entry for a Philip Glasco in Dublin in 1777 is likewise a same-name lead rather than proof for this profile.<ref name="Probate1777">FamilySearch, Dublin probate index entry for Philip Glasco, 1777, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:WGC9-DT2M record WGC9-DT2M].</ref>

[[Glasco-146|Phillip Glasco]] remains a possible duplicate of the elder Dublin watchmaker, not a proved duplicate of this Scottish child. No merge is supported without a record connecting the Scottish family to Dublin.

=== Dublin Glasco namesakes ===
Dublin records include Mrs Glasco in 1760, Mary Glascow in a 1747 probate index and an unidentified Glasco in the Rebellion Papers series. They belong to the wider Dublin Glasco research cluster, but none states a relationship to Philip and none should be attached as his wife or child from surname and place alone.<ref>[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/fdj1725_98.html Underlying record source: mrs glasco].</ref><ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx Underlying record source: mary glascow].</ref><ref>[https://irishmanuscripts.ie/womenshistorysources/index.php?whp_field=collection_code&whp_function=2&whp_searchterm=8830 Underlying record source: unidentified glasco].</ref>
